subject: Hosted API pricing: regional tiering, burst policy, and per-token discounts
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@orchidai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orchidai.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing clarification: regional commit + burst questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Procurement and I are working through the RFP and have a few follow-ups specific to pricing/commits:

- We expect ~4B tokens/mo in US, 1.2B in EU, and occasional spikes ~200-300M in APAC for certain campaigns. How would commits/discounts work across regions? Do we need separate commits per region or can we do a pooled commit?
- If we do a pooled commit, how is the discount applied (blended per-token rate or region-specific tiers)?
- What’s your policy for cross-region bursting? If APAC spikes and draws from US capacity, are there additional cross-region fees or a different rate?
- Invoicing/currency: we invoice in USD but will need VAT treatment for EU usage. Any gotchas there?

Attached is our RFP excerpt (Orchid_RFP_Q1_2026.pdf) with expected volume profiles. Can you provide a short proposal that shows 3 commit options (12mo) and an on-demand fallback?

Cheers,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Infra & Partnerships, Orchid AI

Subject: Re: Pricing clarification: regional commit + burst questions

Hi Emma — thanks for the RFP and the clear volume breakout. Looping in Aditya (pricing/plans) and Vivek (SRE/traffic patterns) so we can give concrete options.

High-level answers up front:
- We support both region-specific commits and a single pooled (global) commit. Pooled commit pricing is simpler (one blended per-token tier) and usually gives better utilization for customers with uneven regional profiles.
- For pooled commits, discounts are applied via tiered thresholds on total tokens consumed across regions; we can show both blended and region-filtered examples.
- Cross-region bursting is allowed by default for pooled commits — there’s no separate "cross-region" surcharge. However, we do have a burst protection policy: sustained cross-region egress beyond the committed monthly average for >72 hours may trigger a temporary throttling/burst-cap fee if it risks capacity for other customers. Short spikes (up to 48 hours) are free within your burst window.
- Invoicing: we bill in USD. EU VAT handling is supported; we’ll emit VAT-only invoices for EU customers and provide tax IDs if needed. We should align with your Finance on invoicing cadence (monthly vs quarterly).

Next steps: Aditya will send 3 concrete pricing options (low/mid/high commit) and a fallback on-demand table. Vivek will add notes on the burst window and recommended burst-protection settings for your profile. I attached a working proposal spreadsheet (Redwood_Proposal_ORCH-1782_v3.xlsx).

Best,

Subject: Re: Pricing clarification: regional commit + burst questions

Emma, Stephanie — a few clarifying details from engineering/pricing side so the proposal can be specific: 

1) Metering & blended rates
- Tokens are metered at request-time by region; for a pooled commit we aggregate usage daily and apply tier discounts at settlement. The customer sees per-region usage on the Console but a single blended rate on the invoice if pooled commit chosen.

2) Commit buckets & roll-over
- Commit tiers are monthly-averaged over the term (12mo). We offer limited month-to-month roll-over up to 10% of committed tokens to absorb seasonal dips — anything beyond is charged at on-demand rates or can be moved to the next month with approval.

3) Burst policy specifics
- Burst window: baseline burst allowance = 30% of your monthly commit available as short-term capacity, measured as a rolling 48-hour peak. For APAC-like spikes that last beyond 72 hours we require either temporary burst capacity reservation (additional fee) or we throttle to sustainable throughput to protect cluster SLAs.
- If you anticipate >300M frequent APAC spikes, we recommend a small regional reserve commit for APAC (e.g., 250M tokens/mo) combined with a global pooled commit — that keeps costs lower than repeated temporary reservations.

4) Currency & taxes
- We invoice USD. For EU VAT we can issue reverse-charge or VAT invoices; we’ll capture your VAT ID during contracting.

I updated the attached spreadsheet with three bucket examples and a blended vs region-separated pricing comparison (see tab: "Geo-Options").

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Procurement/Legal: 

- Can you provide a concrete per-token table for the three commit tiers (monthly tokens) showing: list price, committed discounted price, and blended pooled price for our expected volumes? Please show US/EU/APAC columns and a pooled column.
- For the burst window, can you confirm the invoice treatment if we exceed the burst allowance? Is there a per-token overage rate or a flat temporary reservation fee?
- Currency risk: we prefer USD invoicing but need clarity on whether any region-specific egress fees (e.g., APAC) might be billed separately in local currency.

If you can get a marked-up proposal back by EOD Friday we can escalate to Legal for an initial pass.

Emma

--Procurement note: Orchid prefers a monthly true-up and net-30 payment terms.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@orchidai.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@orchidai.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing clarification: regional commit + burst questions

Emma / Procurement / Legal — attaching a marked proposal and the short MSA snippet for the burst policy (proposed-MSA-snippet.txt). Summary of options (high level):

1) Conservative (12mo) — 3.5B tokens/mo commit (pooled):
   - List price: $0.00040/token (no commit)
   - Committed blended price: $0.00018/token (applies to total pooled usage)
   - Per-region breakout (for reporting only): US $0.00017, EU $0.00019, APAC $0.00020

2) Balanced (12mo) — 5B tokens/mo commit (pooled):
   - Committed blended price: $0.00014/token
   - Per-region guidance: US $0.00013, EU $0.00015, APAC $0.00016

3) Aggressive (12mo) — 7B tokens/mo commit (pooled):
   - Committed blended price: $0.00011/token
   - Per-region guidance: US $0.00010, EU $0.00012, APAC $0.00013

Burst / overage treatment:
- Short spikes within the 48-hour rolling window are free.
- If usage exceeds rolling 48-hour allowance and is sustained >72 hours, we will apply temporary reserved capacity at a flat fee that covers the incremental compute allocation. The fee is negotiated per-event but we typically charge an estimated temporary reservation fee equal to (expected tokens above allowance * 75% of the on-demand list price) unless you pre-purchase a small regional reserve. We included an example calculation in the spreadsheet.

Invoicing & taxes:
- All invoices in USD, monthly true-up, net-30. EU VAT: we can issue VAT invoices or reverse-charge based on your VAT ID. No separate local-currency egress billing unless you specifically request local currency invoicing for APAC.

Next steps: If Procurement/LegaL is comfortable we can:
- Lock option 2 (Balanced) as a starting point and prepare a draft SOW + MSA (I attached the MSA snippet).
- Or schedule a 30-min call early next week to walk through the sheet and the burst examples.

HubSpot: I updated the deal (ORCH-1782) with the Balanced option profile for Legal review: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers if you want to shift more tokens to an APAC reserve vs pooled commits.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
